classification.difficultyReason: Model two angles of elevation, apply the tangent difference identity and simplify an algebraic fraction to prove the stated result.

content.prompt:
A person stands $x$ metres away from a 6-metre-tall billboard placed 2 metres above the ground as shown.

The viewing angle $\theta$ is the difference in angle of elevation from the observer to the top and the base of the billboard.

Show that $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6x}{x^2+16}\right)$.

spec.description: Observer A is left of the vertical support OC. Dashed sight lines AB and AC enclose the viewing angle at A. The billboard extends from B to C. Ground distance AO and vertical distances OB and BC have dimension arrows. The right angle is at O. Decorative brick texture is omitted; the support and billboard remain editable unfilled outlines.
spec.mathematics: AO=x metres, OB=2 metres, BC=6 metres, OC=8 metres, AO perpendicular to OC, and theta=angle BAC.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, dimensions and labels are permanent question givens; no solution annotations are included.

answer.worked:
Let $\alpha$ be the angle of elevation to the top of the billboard and $\beta$ the angle of elevation to its base.

$$\begin{aligned}\tan\alpha&=\frac{8}{x}\\\tan\beta&=\frac{2}{x}\\\theta&=\alpha-\beta\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\tan(\alpha-\beta)\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}{1+\tan\alpha\tan\beta}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\frac{8}{x}-\frac{2}{x}}{1+\left(\frac{8}{x}\right)\left(\frac{2}{x}\right)}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\frac{6}{x}}{1+\frac{16}{x^2}}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\frac{6}{x}}{\frac{x^2+16}{x^2}}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{6}{x}\times\frac{x^2}{x^2+16}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{6x}{x^2+16}\end{aligned}$$

Since $x>0$ and $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, taking the principal inverse tangent gives

$$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6x}{x^2+16}\right).$$
